newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to introduce dlr-denominated trade insurance.
newsitem.headline: Japan to introduce dlr-denominated trade insurance.

text.p: Japan will introduce dollar-denominated trade insurance for large-scale overseas project finance schemes from as early as October, an official at the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Tuesday.
Currently, trade insurance offered by MITI is denominated in yen and is affected by currency fluctuations, as most overseas project finance schemes are carried out in dollars.
The introduction of a dollar-denominated system will solve that, the official said, adding that demand for such a system is greatest for long-term, large-scale projects.
He said the ministry will begin talks on the scheme with those who might seek such insurance in October and implement it as soon as possible.
Under the new system, insurance premiums will be paid in yen, but they will be linked to the exchange rate and be revised each year to reflect it accurately, the official said.

He also said the insurance premium will most likely be higher than in the present yen-denominated system due to higher costs, but thought this would not pose a problem for users. "The merits outweigh the demerits," he said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-5473-3710)
